name: Hajiji Noor
_note: M2 state-executive cohort: Premier (Chief Minister) of Sabah since 29 Sep 2020 (second term sworn 30 Nov 2025). Added as a GOVERNMENT-aligned (GRS) sub-national executive so the new class spans coalitions for the role-controlled partisan-signal gate. NO coder panel yet, so Layer B is unscored and below ranking validity. Anchor values pending an independent coder panel (minCodersToScore=3). Citations verified via search; full text not opened (fetch restriction); reconfirm against primary sources. ACCURACY NOTE: in the 2025 Sabah mining-licence matter the MACC chief affirmatively stated Hajiji was not involved; two assemblymen (not the Premier) were charged. His A5 is none-on-record. B5 left unscored (Kaamatan unity addresses are rhetorical, not adjudicated findings).

metrics.justification: Hajiji has not been charged, arrested, or named a suspect in the Sabah mining-licence matter; on 10 Apr 2025 the MACC chief commissioner stated he was not involved and had cooperated, while two assemblymen and a businessman (not the Premier) were charged on 30 Jun 2025. Recorded as the subject's own status: none on record; a matter involving other officials is not recorded against him.

citation.title: Rest assured, Hajiji not involved in Sabah mining licence case, says MACC chief

metrics.justification: During the mid-2024 Sabah floods he activated the State Disaster Management Committee for cash and food relief and welcomed RM25 million in federal aid (with RM1,000 per affected family), and ahead of the subsequent monsoon stated the state was on standby with 14,209 personnel and 1,456 logistics units. Documented preparedness and relief response (anchor 3).

citation.title: Hajiji welcomes RM25 million aid to repair infrastructure, assist flood victims in Sabah

metrics.justification: The Commercial Collaboration Agreement with Petronas (signed 7 Dec 2021) gave Sabah, via state vehicle SMJ Energy, equity participation and revenue-sharing in oil and gas, with measurable downstream stakes (a 50% interest in the Samarang PSC, 25% in Samur, 25% in ZLNG) and rising MA63 interim special grants. A delivered, measurable participation reform (anchor 3).

citation.title: Sabah and PETRONAS sign Commercial Collaboration Agreement

metrics.justification: On 25 May 2023 the Sabah Legislative Assembly passed the Constitution of the State of Sabah (Amendment) Enactment 2023, an anti-party-hopping law, with 75 assemblymen in support, and he subsequently formalised a cross-coalition GRS-Pakatan Harapan governing alliance. Documented institution-building and cross-bench consensus (anchor 3).

In May 2026 he announced Sabah would defer implementation of the federal border-control agency (MCBA/AKPS) policy pending assurances that Sabah's immigration autonomy under MA63 would not be eroded, a reversal of the earlier posture toward implementation that was publicly welcomed by the state immigration officers' union. A reversal explained on the record (anchor 3).

citation.title: Hajiji: Sabah to defer MCBA policy over immigration rights concerns
